newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power softer on warmer weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power softer on warmer weather.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. ended Wednesday softer than Tuesday's levels on outlook of weather moderating from a recent cold snap.
"Our weather forecast show we will warm up tomorrow. We expect prices to moderate," a South Carolina utility executive said.

Peak, firm power for Thursday delivery into northwestern portion of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) territory were valued at $25.00-$28.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), off from Tuesday's $29.00-$30.00 range.
Firm, next-day power for delivery into northwestern TVA during Thursday's light load hours was pegged at $14.50-$15.00, down from Tuesday's $15.00-$16.00.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices for Thursday were mostly discussed at $25.00-$31.00, with most deals heard done in the $26.00-$28.00 range.
Today's values at the Ga./Fla. border compared with Tuesday's $31.00-$34.00.
Firm, off-peak at the Ga./Fla. border for next-day delivery held steady at $16.00-$18.00.
Peak, firm power scheduled for Thursday delivery in the Florida pennisula ended near $23.50 after talked as high as $28.00 in early trading, traders and marketers said.

The latest forecasts showed temperatures in the Southeast excluding Florida on Thursday would peak in 40s-60s Fahrenheit, and bottom in 20s-30s. In the Florida pennisula, temperatures on Thursday would peak in the 70s-80s and bottom in the 40s-50s.
